subject: Share admitted segmented native images between hosted application profiles
claim: On the 82115-byte enum-request tool workload, packaging profiles 7 and 8 through the prior cache took 27260 ms on Windows and 34749 ms on Debian. Sharing the native image reduced those observations to 23684 and 31628 ms. Both profiles retain distinct containers, match the uncached output bytes exactly, and execute successfully on each host. This establishes a shared construction boundary, not a complete compiler or repository qualification performance claim.

limitations: Single observations using retained native tool artifacts and fresh cache keys; no controlled clean-machine, large compiler-package, or stable regression-threshold claim. The paired image-producing and container phases were run sequentially within each measured command.

The existing cache pipeline is the before/after baseline. Fresh uncached wrappers were also measured: 29742 ms on Windows and 23870 ms on Debian for both profiles. Cache identity checks can outweigh saved construction on small inputs or the mounted Linux filesystem.

An earlier 261-byte probe matched uncached package bytes and behavior but did not improve timing. A first implementation also rehashed container-only producers for the shared image; separating that dependency boundary reduced the final cache overhead. An initial scratch-layout failure was fixed before the recorded final runs.

The image key binds the WVB, host and declared native producer/validator graph independently of the application profile. Container keys retain the hosted producer graph and profile. The private image checkpoint admits at most sixteen 4 MiB fragments and validates its bounded WVLI header before reading fragments. Behavior results are never cached.

Complete database verification and full compiler, bootstrap, reconstruction and paired-host qualification were not run. The changed-file plan included a 2540-second database owner; the causal shared-validator behavior was checked through its existing focused checkpoint test instead.

The temporary baseline/harness files are diagnostics, not new verifier entry points. Prior cache source reconstruction is described in the source identity. All retained behavioral and malformed-input cases extend the existing cache owner.
Aggregate child-process peak memory was not measured. Node and host versions are recorded for reproducibility; broader toolchain-identity and cache-cost auditing remains part of the active redesign.
